mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE drop > 0.5pp does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over the past three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansionary demand periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face reduced output and potentially higher costs.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decline > 2% does not correlate with subsequent negative impacts on corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% MoM does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, the combination signals a very tight labor market, leading to wage inflation and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200k in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 200k does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the past two months signals a strong demand for housing, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase > 10% does not correlate with subsequent positive impacts on related industries.

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and Real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative, the combination signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of INDPRO < 12-month MA and GDPC1 growth < 0% does not correlate with subsequent recessionary impacts on corporate earnings.
